paths.description: Public entry and age-verification gateway, including first-load consent UI; represents every unauthenticated visit.
Adult confirmation into the marketplace homepage; HAR and mobile layout cover the primary gateway transition and loaded marketplace.
Under-age response and recovery state; verifies age-gate feedback and announcement.
Representative marketplace listing reached through an adult-confirmation transition; covers dense results and scrolling.
Representative classified detail URL discovered in the public sitemap; covers a high-risk entity/detail template.
Editorial/advice index template, distinct from marketplace listings and details.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent wall obscures the age gate and all site content on every fresh load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the CMP occupying the whole viewport before the age question can be used; the only prominent paths are ACCEPT ALL or subscription.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with a compact, accessible consent surface that includes an equally prominent reject/non-personalised path and preserves access to the underlying age gate.

findings.summary: Consent choice is asymmetric: accept tracking or subscribe, with no visible reject-all action.
findings.evidence: The mobile and desktop first viewport offers ACCEPT ALL and SUBSCRIBE NOW while the text says 276 partners; rejection requires hunting in the Privacy Center.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide Reject all beside Accept all with equal visual weight, keep granular settings optional, and avoid coupling access to consent or payment.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is not exposed as a native dialog or ARIA dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found no dialog, [role=dialog], or [aria-modal=true], while screenshots show a modal full-screen interruption implemented by .cmp-root-container.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native <dialog> with a labelled heading, managed focus, Escape/cancel behaviour, and explicit consent actions.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.2 s, FCP 2.5 s, Speed Index 5.8 s and performance 0.67; the independent trace measured LCP 6.74 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritise the LCP resource, reduce consent/CSS startup work, and defer non-critical scripts and styles.

findings.summary: The page ships a long render-blocking chain and excessive startup resources.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 149 requests and 1.36 MB transferred, including 50 scripts and 14 stylesheets; Lighthouse estimated 1,490 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle only route-critical CSS, remove unused widget/editor styles from the gateway, defer non-critical scripts, and split shared Kotlin/RequireJS bundles by route.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused and legacy code are delivered on the simple gateway.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 313 KiB unused JavaScript, 56 KiB unused CSS and 15 KiB legacy JavaScript; the largest script alone transferred 228,788 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route-level code splitting and modern-only output, and do not preload editor, carousel, fancybox, upload, payment, or widget code until those features are requested.

findings.summary: The representative listing performs a severe main-thread long task.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded a 496 ms long task at 5.66 s after navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the listing hydration/render task, chunk result processing, virtualise offscreen work, and yield between batches with scheduler APIs.

findings.summary: No enforcing Content-Security-Policy is sent and one long-lived cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP. Cookies primitive found __ssid without Secure, SameSite=None and a 400-day lifetime; five cookies were flagged by the primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based enforcing CSP, mark every cross-site cookie Secure, minimise SameSite=None usage, and shorten non-essential cookie lifetimes.

findings.evidence: Headers primitive confirmed HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN but reported missing Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; retain HSTS and frame protection.

findings.summary: Nearly the entire network load is classified as cross-origin and the consent wall describes sharing with 276 partners.
findings.evidence: HAR classified 143 of 149 requests and 1.32 MB of 1.36 MB as cross-origin relative to erotik.markt.de; the consent screenshot states 276 partners and usage-based advertising/tracking.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to non-personalised operation, remove unnecessary vendors, proxy same-organisation static assets where appropriate, and load optional advertising/analytics only after freely given consent.

findings.summary: Public entity URLs expose the generic age-confirmation document instead of unique page metadata to fresh crawlers.
findings.evidence: The representative detail DOM returned title and description “Über-18-Bestätigung”; raw-vs-rendered discoverability coverage was only 35%.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render each public route’s unique title, description, heading, canonical and safe textual summary before the age interaction while keeping restricted media gated.

findings.summary: Only 35% of rendered content is present without JavaScript, and a fresh detail route degrades to the generic age gate.
findings.evidence: Discoverability primitive measured 35% raw-content coverage. The crawler screenshot and detail DOM show the gateway rather than route content, although the raw shell itself is non-empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Render safe core route content and semantic links on the server, then progressively enhance gated media and interactions after age confirmation.

findings.evidence: Images primitive found three of five images without width/height; Lighthouse also failed its unsized-images audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height attributes (or equivalent aspect-ratio reservation) to both logo variants and the JUSPROG image.

findings.summary: Animations remain active when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() still returned two running animations; CSS only declared reduced-motion rules for no-preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or greatly shorten non-essential CMP and navigation animation inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: The age-confirmation navigation is an abrupt full-document swap with no visible continuity.
findings.evidence: The transition capture produced only a single stable frame and source probes found no authored view-transition rules, while the adult click caused a full navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for the age-gate-to-marketplace navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The public gateway and fresh route response expose no Open Graph or JSON-LD metadata.
findings.evidence: Recon found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks, while sitemap URLs represent classified entities that benefit from accurate safe previews.
findings.suggestedFix: Add route-accurate Open Graph metadata and safe schema.org JSON-LD for listings and editorial pages without exposing restricted imagery to under-age users.
